allObjections.title: Unbounded recommendation generation risk
allObjections.detail: §7 item #8's minimal envelope lacks any rate limits or caps on recommendation volume. Without PA-1..PA-N invariants, agents could flood operators with thousands of low-quality recommendations per run, creating noise that obscures critical findings.

allObjections.title: Cost estimation without validation
allObjections.detail: The new cost.effort_hours_estimate field in §7 has no validation bounds or accuracy requirements. Agents could emit wildly incorrect estimates (0.1 hours for major refactors, 1000 hours for trivial changes) with no conformance test to catch this.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure underspecified
allObjections.detail: §7's rollback.revert_procedure is a free-text string with no schema or required steps. CA16A-v2-CT-3 only warns on non-revertable accepted recs but doesn't validate that revert_procedure is actually executable or complete.

allObjections.title: Defer-window config lacks audit trail
allObjections.detail: §7 item #8 + §3 admin config allows per-product defer windows [1,365] days but has no requirement to log changes to recommendation_defer_window_days. An admin could set 365-day deferrals to effectively suppress recommendations without trace.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback mechanism in case the Redesign/Build Environment causes unintended changes to the ProductSSOT. This is a significant risk, as it could lead to data loss or corruption. The §29 Redesign/Build Environment section should include a detailed rollback plan to mitigate this risk.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Validation
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient validation rules for the proactive recommendations envelope. The minimal canonical envelope is too permissive, and the full schema deferred to engineering dispatch may not be thoroughly tested. This could lead to invalid or inconsistent data being stored in the ProductSSOT.

allObjections.title: Overly Complex Taxonomy
allObjections.detail: The 6-class Multi-Format taxonomy may be overly complex and difficult to maintain. The proposal should consider a simpler taxonomy or provide a clear justification for the need for six classes. Additionally, the proposal should include a plan for handling new or emerging formats that do not fit into the existing taxonomy.

allObjections.title: Overly Complex Deferral
allObjections.detail: The proposal defers too many critical details to engineering dispatch, such as the full schema invariants (PA-1..PA-N). This deferral could lead to inconsistencies and lack of clarity in the implementation phase. Specifically, §7 item #8 defers the full schema to engineering, which may cause misunderstandings and misalignments.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback Mechanism
allObjections.detail: The proposal introduces a `rollback` object but does not specify a concrete rollback mechanism for accepted recommendations. This could lead to situations where accepted recommendations cannot be safely reverted, causing potential disruptions. The `rollback` object in §7 item #8 should include a mandatory revert procedure.

allObjections.title: Vague Admin Gating
allObjections.detail: The wording for the Redesign/Build Environment (RB-Env) is vague regarding admin gating. It states that RB-Env is admin-gated but does not specify the exact workflow or approval process. This vagueness could lead to misinterpretations and potential security risks. The scope statement in the Redesign/Build Environment section should be more explicit.

allObjections.title: Minimal Envelope Risk
allObjections.detail: The minimal canonical envelope may not capture all necessary details for effective implementation, leading to potential gaps in the proactive recommendations system.

allObjections.title: Defer-Window Complexity
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer-window configuration adds complexity without clear benefits, potentially leading to inconsistent application of recommendations across products.

allObjections.title: Section Number Ambiguity
allObjections.detail: Deferring the section number for the Redesign/Build Environment creates ambiguity and may lead to confusion in the implementation and maintenance of the feature.

allObjections.title: Cost object underspecified
allObjections.detail: The `cost` object in the `proactive_recommendation` schema (§7) lacks concrete guidance on how `effort_hours_estimate`, `risk_tier`, and `blast_radius` should be determined, leading to inconsistent application and potential gaming of the system. The lack of clear definitions for `risk_tier` and `blast_radius` makes them subjective and open to interpretation.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The `rollback` object's `revert_procedure` field (§7) is optional and human-readable, which is insufficient for ensuring reliable reversibility.  Without a standardized, machine-executable rollback mechanism, the system relies on potentially error-prone manual processes, increasing the risk of failed rollbacks and system instability. The 'revertable' boolean alone is insufficient.

allObjections.title: Deferral window clamping risk
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer-window config (§7) clamps out-of-bounds values, but the notification via `agent.product_registry.defer_window_clamped.v1` might be missed by admins, leading to unexpected behavior.  A more prominent warning or blocking mechanism might be necessary to ensure admins are aware of the clamping.

allObjections.title: Ambiguity detection threshold
allObjections.detail: The stricter classifier in CA-16-C-Q2, with a confidence floor of 0.85, might lead to excessive `target_class_ambiguous` findings, overwhelming operators with dispute resolution tasks. The choice of 0.85 seems arbitrary and lacks empirical justification. This could lead to alert fatigue.

allObjections.title: Deferred schema risks divergence
allObjections.detail: CA-16-A v2's deferred full schema to engineering dispatch creates future compatibility risks. Without canonical PA-1..PA-N invariants in §7, engineering implementations may diverge from intent, particularly around mandatory validation rules. This violates SSOT's single-source-of-truth principle and could break conformance tests like CA16A-v2-CT-2.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure inadequacy
allObjections.detail: The new rollback.revert_procedure field (§7 Proactive Recommendations) lacks enforcement mechanisms. Conformance test CA16A-v2-CT-3 only flags non-revertable recs without blocking acceptance. In complex deployments, manual revert steps may be insufficient for stateful changes, risking system instability when reversing implemented recommendations.

allObjections.title: Ambiguity severity inflation
allObjections.detail: CA-16-C v2's stricter classifier (§6 Multi-Format) mandates 'high' severity for target_class_ambiguous at <0.85 confidence. This could flood operators with false-positive high-severity tickets for legitimate hybrid formats like PWAs, diluting attention from genuine critical findings and violating §7.6's severity calibration principles.

allObjections.title: Defer-window governance gap
allObjections.detail: Per-product defer-window (CA-16-A-Q4) allows operators to set 365-day deferrals without admin oversight. This enables indefinite suppression of recommendations via recurrent deferrals, contravening the proactive intent. CA16A-v2-CT-5/6 only validate clamping, not governance of excessive deferral patterns.

allObjections.title: Mandatory fields still undercut optionality
allObjections.detail: In CA-16-A v2, `purpose_record_link` and `market_definition_link` are made optional, but the envelope still requires `category`, `title`, `rationale`, and `source` without defining how null/empty recommendations are represented when the system has only a weak heuristic suggestion. That creates a gap between the claimed “minimal canonical envelope” and real emission paths from §7.6 / §10.1, especially for cross-cutting suggestions that do not map cleanly to a single product or run.

allObjections.title: Rollback is advisory only
allObjections.detail: The new `rollback` object adds `revertable` and `revert_procedure`, but CA16A-v2-CT-3 explicitly says non-revertable accepted recommendations are only “flagged but not blocked.” This preserves the exact failure mode the Panel objected to in v1: operators can still accept recommendations that cannot be safely undone, with no hard gate or enforcement path in the canonical contract.

allObjections.title: Defer-window can hide urgent recs
allObjections.detail: CA-16-A-Q4 moves defer timing into a per-product knob with bounds [1,365], but the spec does not define any escalation or override behavior for high-severity recommendations that are deferred long-term. A product owner could set 365 days and effectively suppress repeated resurfacing of a critical systemic recommendation, which is a concrete governance regression compared with a uniform shorter window.

allObjections.title: RB-Env numbering deferral is incomplete
allObjections.detail: CA-16-B-Q1 defers the section number for Redesign/Build Environment, yet the same block continues to assert canonical scope, atomic-audit-write, and mandatory cross-references to CA-14 fix-safety invariants. This creates a half-canonical surface: implementers must wire behavior now, but the spec avoids the one piece that anchors documentation and review navigation, increasing divergence risk across mirrored copies and later amendments.

allObjections.title: Silent fallback removed without evidence
allObjections.detail: CA-16-C-Q2 tightens classification by emitting `target_class_ambiguous.v1` whenever confidence <0.85, but the proposal does not specify calibration data, class priors, or how to handle known ambiguous hybrids like PWA/SaaS shells beyond operator dispute resolution. That can convert previously working generic fallbacks into a high-severity alert storm, increasing manual workload without proving better classification accuracy.

allObjections.title: Unclear Impact of Cost Object
allObjections.detail: The new 'cost' object in proactive recommendations (§7 item #8) includes 'effort_hours_estimate', 'risk_tier', and 'blast_radius'. However, it's unclear how these fields will be used in practice and how they will affect the decision-making process for operators.

allObjections.title: Rollback Mechanism Ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The 'rollback' object is introduced with a 'revertable' boolean and an optional 'revert_procedure'. The proposal lacks clarity on how this will be enforced or validated, particularly for complex recommendations.

allObjections.title: Defer-Window Config Flexibility
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer-window configuration (§7 item #8 + §3 admin config) allows for a wide range of values ([1,365] days). This flexibility might lead to inconsistent practices across different products and operators.

allObjections.title: Minimal envelope omits validation
allObjections.detail: §7 item #8 defines cost.risk_tier and rollback.revertable but states full schema invariants (PA-1..PA-N) are deferred to engineering dispatch; no canonical rule enforces atomicity with ProductSSOT delta_log writes per §7.5.

allObjections.title: Stricter classifier lacks workflow
allObjections.detail: CA-16-C-v2-Q2 requires target_class_ambiguous at high severity for confidence <0.85 yet provides no operator dispute resolution path or tie-in to §6 deliberate error-state triggers or §11 ClearanceRecord steps.

allObjections.title: Per-product defer desync risk
allObjections.detail: CA-16-A-Q4 adds recommendation_defer_window_days to product_registry without mandating atomic update alongside proactive_recommendation.disposition in the same run, violating the atomic guarantee claimed in §7.5.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: The v2 minimal envelope with deferred schema creates a two-tier system where critical validation lives outside canonical SSOT, allowing engineering to ship recommendation generators that emit unbounded, unvalidated suggestions that could overwhelm operators worse than having no recommendations at all.
adversarial.precedent: Kubernetes' early CRD (Custom Resource Definition) system allowed arbitrary schemas without validation, leading to operators being flooded with malformed resources that crashed controllers - they had to retrofit OpenAPI validation in v1.16 to fix the damage.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal fragments governance by moving critical invariants (PA-1..PA-N) out of canonical SSOT into engineering dispatch, creating a dangerous precedent where safety controls can be modified without Panel oversight. Combined with the elimination of recommendations from §11 Clearance flow, this creates an ungoverned side-channel that could emit arbitrary volumes of unvalidated suggestions, fundamentally undermining the SSOT's role as the single source of truth for system behavior.

CA-16-A-v2-Q1.rationale: The minimal envelope without rate limits, validation rules, or generation bounds creates an ungoverned surface that could flood operators with noise, requiring full invariants in canonical.

CA-16-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Despite concerns about ungoverned side-channels, keeping recommendations outside the critical clearance path prevents them from blocking product delivery.

CA-16-A-v2-Q3.rationale: The current lifecycle lacks reversibility for mistaken rejections; adding reopen state provides necessary flexibility while maintaining audit trail.

CA-16-A-v2-Q4.pick_text: Ratify with stricter bounds — [7,90] instead of [1,365].
CA-16-A-v2-Q4.rationale: A 365-day defer window effectively equals permanent suppression; [7,90] maintains the per-product flexibility while preventing recommendation burial.

CA-16-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — RB-Env should not be canonical yet; defer whole surface to later CA-N.
CA-16-B-v2-Q1.rationale: The surface is clearly underspecified per Panel objections #9,#16,#20,#24,#26; canonicalizing even the scope statement without the implementation details is premature.

CA-16-B-v2-Q2.pick_text: Reject — wording is too vague; needs concrete operator workflow spec in canonical.
CA-16-B-v2-Q2.rationale: "Operator-steerable rebuild" provides no concrete workflow, state machine, or interaction model; this vagueness will create implementation divergence.

CA-16-C-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — defer canonical taxonomy until ≥1 product per class is in ProductSSOT.
CA-16-C-v2-Q1.rationale: Canonicalizing a 6-class taxonomy before validating it against real products risks creating categories that don't match actual usage patterns.

CA-16-C-v2-Q2.rationale: Given the high severity of ambiguous classification and lack of real-world validation of the classifier, a 0.90 floor provides better safety margin against misclassification.

CA-16-C-v2-Q3.pick_text: Defer — ownership belongs in agent registry, not canonical SSOT spec.
CA-16-C-v2-Q3.rationale: Agent ownership is an implementation detail that changes as agents evolve; embedding Agent #21 ownership in canonical spec creates unnecessary coupling.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal makes reasonable progress, but some areas require further refinement, particularly the cost and rollback objects in proactive recommendations and the scope of the Redesign/Build Environment.

objections.title: Deferred schema risks divergence
objections.detail: CA-16-A v2's deferred full schema to engineering dispatch creates future compatibility risks. Without canonical PA-1..PA-N invariants in §7, engineering implementations may diverge from intent, particularly around mandatory validation rules. This violates SSOT's single-source-of-truth principle and could break conformance tests like CA16A-v2-CT-2.

objections.title: Rollback procedure inadequacy
objections.detail: The new rollback.revert_procedure field (§7 Proactive Recommendations) lacks enforcement mechanisms. Conformance test CA16A-v2-CT-3 only flags non-revertable recs without blocking acceptance. In complex deployments, manual revert steps may be insufficient for stateful changes, risking system instability when reversing implemented recommendations.

objections.title: Ambiguity severity inflation
objections.detail: CA-16-C v2's stricter classifier (§6 Multi-Format) mandates 'high' severity for target_class_ambiguous at <0.85 confidence. This could flood operators with false-positive high-severity tickets for legitimate hybrid formats like PWAs, diluting attention from genuine critical findings and violating §7.6's severity calibration principles.

objections.title: Defer-window governance gap
objections.detail: Per-product defer-window (CA-16-A-Q4) allows operators to set 365-day deferrals without admin oversight. This enables indefinite suppression of recommendations via recurrent deferrals, contravening the proactive intent. CA16A-v2-CT-5/6 only validate clamping, not governance of excessive deferral patterns.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: Under the new proactive recommendations system, an operator could accept a non-revertable recommendation (rollback.revertable=false) with underestimated cost (effort_hours_estimate), then encounter cascading failures during implementation. With no clearance gate (Step 1.5 removed), this could degrade system stability beyond the current zero-recommendation baseline, as status quo lacks this failure vector entirely.
adversarial.precedent: Google Health's 2008-2011 failure featured proactive recommendations without cost/rollback fields, leading to clinician rejection due to unquantified workflow disruption and irreversibility concerns—parallels CA-16-A's risk profile.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal introduces significant unquantified risks: deferred schemas invite implementation drift, per-product defer-windows enable recommendation suppression, and stricter ambiguity classification may overwhelm operators. Until cost/rollback fields receive enforcement parity with clearance gates, and classifier thresholds gain empirical validation, deferring CA-16 preserves stability while avoiding new governance gaps.

CA-16-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (minimal envelope + 2 new fields; full schema deferred)
CA-16-A-v2-Q1.rationale: Minimal envelope addresses core objections while allowing engineering flexibility; conditional mandatory links would reintroduce v1's over-constraint issues.

CA-16-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Eliminating Step 1.5 avoids clearance pipeline bloat; side-channel surfacing aligns with non-blocking intent while reducing operator cognitive load.

CA-16-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (same lifecycle as v1)
CA-16-A-v2-Q3.rationale: Lifecycle states provide necessary granularity; adding reopen would complicate disposition tracking without addressing core adversarial concerns.

CA-16-A-v2-Q4.pick_text: Ratify with stricter bounds — [7,90] instead of [1,365]
CA-16-A-v2-Q4.rationale: [1,365] range enables dangerous suppression via year-long defers; [7,90] bounds prevent evasion while preserving operational flexibility.

CA-16-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (section number = engineering decision)
CA-16-B-v2-Q1.rationale: Section numbering is cosmetic; deferral avoids premature canonicalization while preserving RB-Env's functional invariants.

CA-16-B-v2-Q2.rationale: Wording sufficiently conveys steerable nature; adding explicit admin approval language would duplicate §11.7's existing RB-7 controls.

CA-16-C-v2-Q1.rationale: Taxonomy covers observed formats; merging web/mobile_app ignores PWA distinctness, while splitting agentic_ai is premature without evidence.

CA-16-C-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (0.85 floor; ambiguity emits `high`)
CA-16-C-v2-Q2.rationale: 0.85 balances strictness and practicality; 0.90 would increase false positives, while 0.75 or silent fallback would undermine detection rigor.

CA-16-C-v2-Q3.rationale: Ownership aligns with existing Phase B responsibilities; creating new agents or co-ownership would introduce fragmentation without clear benefit.

perReviewer.overallNotes: V2 improvements address key rerun objections, but enforcement gaps in rollback/cost fields warrant future scrutiny.

objections.title: Mandatory fields still undercut optionality
objections.detail: In CA-16-A v2, `purpose_record_link` and `market_definition_link` are made optional, but the envelope still requires `category`, `title`, `rationale`, and `source` without defining how null/empty recommendations are represented when the system has only a weak heuristic suggestion. That creates a gap between the claimed “minimal canonical envelope” and real emission paths from §7.6 / §10.1, especially for cross-cutting suggestions that do not map cleanly to a single product or run.

objections.title: Rollback is advisory only
objections.detail: The new `rollback` object adds `revertable` and `revert_procedure`, but CA16A-v2-CT-3 explicitly says non-revertable accepted recommendations are only “flagged but not blocked.” This preserves the exact failure mode the Panel objected to in v1: operators can still accept recommendations that cannot be safely undone, with no hard gate or enforcement path in the canonical contract.

objections.title: Defer-window can hide urgent recs
objections.detail: CA-16-A-Q4 moves defer timing into a per-product knob with bounds [1,365], but the spec does not define any escalation or override behavior for high-severity recommendations that are deferred long-term. A product owner could set 365 days and effectively suppress repeated resurfacing of a critical systemic recommendation, which is a concrete governance regression compared with a uniform shorter window.

objections.title: RB-Env numbering deferral is incomplete
objections.detail: CA-16-B-Q1 defers the section number for Redesign/Build Environment, yet the same block continues to assert canonical scope, atomic-audit-write, and mandatory cross-references to CA-14 fix-safety invariants. This creates a half-canonical surface: implementers must wire behavior now, but the spec avoids the one piece that anchors documentation and review navigation, increasing divergence risk across mirrored copies and later amendments.

objections.title: Silent fallback removed without evidence
objections.detail: CA-16-C-Q2 tightens classification by emitting `target_class_ambiguous.v1` whenever confidence <0.85, but the proposal does not specify calibration data, class priors, or how to handle known ambiguous hybrids like PWA/SaaS shells beyond operator dispute resolution. That can convert previously working generic fallbacks into a high-severity alert storm, increasing manual workload without proving better classification accuracy.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If a team sets a long defer window for a product and the system repeatedly defers a high-value recommendation while RB-Env changes are partially wired but section-numbered later, operators get noisier governance, less traceability, and more ambiguous ownership than the status quo. Instead of a simple fixed window and stable section anchors, reviewers may spend time reconciling missing canonical references while important suggestions stay hidden for months.
adversarial.precedent: GitHub’s long-running issues around ambiguous markdown/JSON handling and Docusaurus discussions on malformed code-block rendering show how “minimal canonical envelope now, schema later” often creates interoperability pain and parser drift. More directly, many systems that tried advisory-only safety flags before hard enforcement, such as warning-only release gates, saw operators routinely accept risky items that the warnings did not actually prevent.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring this proposal is that it still mixes canonical commitments with intentionally deferred schema details, leaving too much behavior to engineering judgment. The added cost and rollback fields help, but they do not close the enforcement gap for non-revertable recommendations or ambiguous multi-format classification, so the amendment may increase governance complexity without materially reducing risk. A clean deferral until the full recommendation schema, rollback semantics, and ownership model are specified would likely be safer and easier to implement consistently.

CA-16-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (minimal envelope + 2 new fields; full schema deferred).
CA-16-A-v2-Q1.rationale: This is the only option that matches the draft’s explicit minimal-envelope approach while preserving the new cost and rollback fields. The proposal is incomplete, but internally it clearly intends deferment rather than full canonicalization.

CA-16-A-v2-Q2.rationale: The draft consistently removes Step 1.5 and routes recommendations to a side-channel governance surface. Even if risky, this is the proposal’s stated design and the question asks for that specific ratification.

CA-16-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (same lifecycle as v1).
CA-16-A-v2-Q3.rationale: The disposition states are preserved from v1 and remain the only concrete lifecycle defined here. The draft does not provide a better alternative with clearer operational semantics.

CA-16-A-v2-Q4.rationale: The per-product defer-window is explicitly specified with default, bounds, and admin configurability. While I object to edge cases, the proposed configuration model itself is internally coherent.

CA-16-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (section number = engineering decision).
CA-16-B-v2-Q1.rationale: The draft intentionally defers numbering to engineering dispatch and keeps the surface-name stable. That is consistent with the proposal’s own change log and avoids premature section anchoring.

CA-16-B-v2-Q2.rationale: The wording is vague, but it is clearly marked as carry-forward and the concrete approval gate is handled elsewhere in the referenced cleared material. On this narrow question, the draft preserves the existing phraseology.

CA-16-C-v2-Q1.rationale: The six-class taxonomy is explicit and stable across the draft. The stricter ambiguity handling belongs to the classifier question, not the class list itself.

CA-16-C-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (0.85 floor; ambiguity emits `high`).
CA-16-C-v2-Q2.rationale: The proposal squarely tightens detection at the stated threshold and makes ambiguity visible instead of silently falling back. That is the specific change under review here.

CA-16-C-v2-Q3.rationale: The draft assigns ownership directly and frames it as a coherent extension of an already-cleared scope. No alternative in the options is better supported by the text.

perReviewer.overallNotes: I’m voting within the draft’s stated structures, but the proposal still feels under-specified in enforcement terms, especially around non-revertable recommendations and ambiguous format classification.

objections.title: Unclear Impact of Cost Object
objections.detail: The new 'cost' object in proactive recommendations (§7 item #8) includes 'effort_hours_estimate', 'risk_tier', and 'blast_radius'. However, it's unclear how these fields will be used in practice and how they will affect the decision-making process for operators.

objections.title: Rollback Mechanism Ambiguity
objections.detail: The 'rollback' object is introduced with a 'revertable' boolean and an optional 'revert_procedure'. The proposal lacks clarity on how this will be enforced or validated, particularly for complex recommendations.

objections.title: Defer-Window Config Flexibility
objections.detail: The per-product defer-window configuration (§7 item #8 + §3 admin config) allows for a wide range of values ([1,365] days). This flexibility might lead to inconsistent practices across different products and operators.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the proactive recommendations are not properly filtered or prioritized, they might overwhelm operators with low-value suggestions, potentially leading to decision fatigue and decreased effectiveness of the FlowAI system.
adversarial.precedent: A similar design in a previous project led to information overload for operators, resulting in decreased adoption of the recommendation system.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal could be rejected or deferred due to the lack of clear guidelines on how the new 'cost' and 'rollback' objects will be utilized and enforced in practice, potentially leading to inconsistent application and reduced effectiveness.

CA-16-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (minimal envelope + 2 new fields; full schema deferred).
CA-16-A-v2-Q1.rationale: The minimal envelope with new fields for cost and rollback seems like a reasonable step forward, and deferring the full schema to engineering dispatch allows for more detailed specification.

CA-16-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Removing proactive recommendations from the §11 Clearance flow could streamline the clearance process, but it's crucial to ensure that recommendations are still effectively communicated to operators.

CA-16-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (same lifecycle as v1).
CA-16-A-v2-Q3.rationale: The disposition lifecycle as drafted seems comprehensive, covering various states that a recommendation can be in, which is beneficial for tracking and managing recommendations.

CA-16-A-v2-Q4.pick_text: Ratify with stricter bounds — [7,90] instead of [1,365].
CA-16-A-v2-Q4.rationale: While per-product defer-window configuration is useful, stricter bounds could prevent extreme values that might not be practical or effective.

CA-16-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (section number = engineering decision).
CA-16-B-v2-Q1.rationale: Deferring the section number to engineering dispatch makes sense as it allows for flexibility in the final placement based on the overall structure decided by the engineering team.

CA-16-B-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify with stronger admin-gating wording — "operator initiates; admin approves".
CA-16-B-v2-Q2.rationale: Clarifying the roles in the Redesign/Build Environment process with stronger admin-gating wording could improve the governance and control over the rebuild process.

CA-16-C-v2-Q1.rationale: The 6-class taxonomy for Multi-Format targets seems comprehensive and covers various types of applications and services, which is beneficial for classification purposes.

CA-16-C-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (0.85 floor; ambiguity emits `high`).
CA-16-C-v2-Q2.rationale: The stricter classifier confidence floor and the handling of ambiguity at 'high' severity seem like a balanced approach to ensure both accuracy and caution in classification.

CA-16-C-v2-Q3.rationale: Assigning ownership of Multi-Format target classification to Agent #21, as per the existing scope in CA-14-A-Q3, maintains consistency and leverages the capabilities of this agent.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal addresses several concerns from the previous version and refines the specifications for proactive recommendations, Redesign/Build Environment, and Multi-Format targets. However, the effectiveness of these changes depends on the detailed implementation and operational practices.

objections.title: Minimal envelope omits validation
objections.detail: §7 item #8 defines cost.risk_tier and rollback.revertable but states full schema invariants (PA-1..PA-N) are deferred to engineering dispatch; no canonical rule enforces atomicity with ProductSSOT delta_log writes per §7.5.

objections.title: Stricter classifier lacks workflow
objections.detail: CA-16-C-v2-Q2 requires target_class_ambiguous at high severity for confidence <0.85 yet provides no operator dispute resolution path or tie-in to §6 deliberate error-state triggers or §11 ClearanceRecord steps.

objections.title: Per-product defer desync risk
objections.detail: CA-16-A-Q4 adds recommendation_defer_window_days to product_registry without mandating atomic update alongside proactive_recommendation.disposition in the same run, violating the atomic guarantee claimed in §7.5.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: Per-product defer windows plus deferred schema could produce stale or conflicting recommendation states across environments when a run updates ProductSSOT but the defer computation lags, creating more operator confusion than the prior fixed 14-day global rule.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The v2 draft defers too many critical mechanisms (full schema, section numbering, dispute workflows) to later engineering dispatches while still claiming canonical status for partial envelopes; this fragments the SSOT and weakens the safety invariants that CA-14-B and §10 Self-Heal were meant to enforce, making outright rejection or full deferral to a later complete CA cycle the safer choice.

CA-16-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — proactive recs envelope should be canonical complete OR not canonical at all.
CA-16-A-v2-Q1.rationale: Partial envelope with deferred validation directly creates the enforcement gap named in objection 1.

CA-16-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Eliminating the step while leaving recommendations as an unintegrated side-channel increases operator overhead without clearance gating.

CA-16-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: Defer entirely — lifecycle state machine belongs in engineering dispatch.
CA-16-A-v2-Q3.rationale: Lifecycle interacts with the still-deferred defer-window logic and should not be frozen in canonical text yet.

CA-16-A-v2-Q4.pick_text: Reject — global fixed 14-day window simpler and sufficient.
CA-16-A-v2-Q4.rationale: Per-product config adds desync surface without atomicity guarantees, as flagged in objection 3.

CA-16-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — RB-Env should not be canonical yet; defer whole surface to later CA-N.
CA-16-B-v2-Q1.rationale: Naming the surface while deferring its section and full spec repeats the fragmentation problem.

CA-16-B-v2-Q2.pick_text: Reject — wording is too vague; needs concrete operator workflow spec in canonical.
CA-16-B-v2-Q2.rationale: Steerable rebuild language lacks the RB-7 conformance detail required for admin-only gate.

CA-16-C-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — defer canonical taxonomy until ≥1 product per class is in ProductSSOT.
CA-16-C-v2-Q1.rationale: 6-class taxonomy is premature given the stricter classifier's ambiguity handling is still underspecified.

CA-16-C-v2-Q2.pick_text: Reject — restore v1 silent fallback to `generic_url`.
CA-16-C-v2-Q2.rationale: 0.85 floor with mandatory high-severity findings will flood operators without defined resolution paths.

CA-16-C-v2-Q3.pick_text: Defer — ownership belongs in agent registry, not canonical SSOT spec.
CA-16-C-v2-Q3.rationale: Agent #21 ownership claim should follow the same deferral discipline applied to schemas and section numbers.

perReviewer.overallNotes: Multiple deferrals undermine the claim that v2 is a stable canonical increment.
